messages:
maya chen: Heads up — ACME reported a sudden 3x jump in embedding counts after upgrading to vendor-sdk v2.1. They attached logs, saying their usage pattern didn't change.
juan ramos: thanks. can you paste a short sample of the logs? wondering if it's a client-side duplicate send.
maya chen: snippet from ACME logs: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings 200 92ms tokens=0 embeds=1 id=abc123
POST /v1/embeddings 200 95ms tokens=0 embeds=1 id=abc123
```
maya chen: they show identical ids repeating within ~150ms windows. looks like the third-party SDK retries without de-duping request ids.
kevin li: that would cause double-counting in our ingest if we count per-request. is there a request-id header we could use to dedupe?
maya chen: vendor-sdk v2.1 started sending an X-req-id but with different header name intermittently (x-request-id / X-Req-Id). their metadata team says they normalized it but it's inconsistent for some clients.
sarah patel: do we have a quick mitigation? can we ignore duplicate embed writes by payload hash for a short window?
kevin li: we can add a 1s in-memory dedupe on request-id + model + customer_id at the edge. low-risk. I'll put up a rollout.
juan ramos: how many affected customers and what is the estimated overcount? ACME says ~22k extra embeds in last billing hour.
maya chen: ACME account id: acme-inc. Our preliminary ledger shows +21,980 embeds between 2026-02-28T09:00 and 10:00 UTC.
sarah patel: rough $ impact?
kevin li: at $0.0004/embed -> ~$8.8. small per hour but recurring. but several mid-market customers on same SDK could add up.
maya chen: ACME requesting an invoice adjustment and a backfill to remove duplicates in their ledger.
juan ramos: if the duplicates are provable via duplicate request-id or identical payload+id, we can run a targeted backfill. need approvals for: (1) run backfill job, (2) issue provisional credit while backfill runs.
sarah patel: finance: +1 for provisional credit up to $20 for this window pending audit. approve?
kevin li: I'll open infra ticket MET-4321 with the dedupe patch and backfill job plan. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/785. plan: 1) short-term edge dedupe rollout (canary), 2) ledger backfill that removes events with duplicate (request-id || payload-hash) within 2s per customer, 3) audit report.
maya chen: ACME agrees to let us run backfill and share logs.
juan ramos: accounting: please run SQL to compute exact duplicate set and delta. proposed query: 
```
SELECT customer_id, count(*) AS total, count(DISTINCT coalesce(request_id, sha256(payload))) AS unique_events, count(*) - count(DISTINCT coalesce(request_id, sha256(payload))) AS duplicates
FROM embed_events
WHERE customer_id = 'acme-inc' AND timestamp >= '2026-02-28 09:00:00' AND timestamp < '2026-02-28 11:00:00'
GROUP BY customer_id;
```
billing-bot: Audit run queued: job_id=aud-9982. ETA 14m.
sarah patel: great. provisional credit approved for ACME up to $25 while audit completes — finance ticket FIN-2129. Please attach the audit output before final credit.
kevin li: noted. I'll coordinate with infra and ops. timeline: edge dedupe in next 4h canary, backfill in 24h after audit result.
maya chen: tagging @juan ramos for final signoff on invoice memo to ACME.
juan ramos: signed off. please cc billing@acme on the memo and include the mitigation timeline and refund mechanics.
sarah patel: leaving a note — if backfill uncovers broader vendor SDK impact, we'll cap credits at customer-level review and escalate to vendor for root-cause fix and possible reimbursements.
kevin li: will add vendor escalation ticket VND-117 and ask for SDK patch with consistent X-req-id header behavior.
maya chen: thanks all — closing this thread once MET-4321 and FIN-2129 created and linked in thread.
